items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: Hardy, myself and Frisco. Her husband was the piano player, Al Segal. And that's all in five pieces.

ctx.x: you know. Oh you didn't? I think like some parade, like Contessa Antiglia, would be posed in front of the church. And they'd all line up in front of the church.

And we used to play the Italian all the time. But I didn't stay too long with the Italian band, because I started playing with these Dixieland bands. And then when I quit playing with the Dixieland, I went to play vaudeville. And then I went to Chicago with this B. Palmer, the shimmy shaker that came from Chicago. She took Rapport, Emmett Hardy, you know those boys. Frisco, Johnny Frisco. And we played vaudeville. And in fact, that's where the New Orleans Rhythm Kings started.
